sections.label: Our Teams

briefs.headline: Chelsea beat Leeds 6-3 after trailing 2-0 at the break in the Carabao Cup
briefs.summary: Leeds led through Tarik Muharemovic's 23rd-minute header and Brenden Aaronson in the 48th before Xabi Alonso's four halftime changes turned it at Stamford Bridge: Cole Palmer scored a 53rd-minute penalty and again in the 55th, Pedro Neto in the 60th, Danny Welbeck in the 65th and in stoppage time, and Valentin Barco his first Chelsea goal in the 80th; Dominic Calvert-Lewin pulled one back for Leeds. Morgan Rogers assisted four. 'I take responsibility with the first half,' Alonso said. Chelsea advance to the fourth round.

briefs.headline: Liverpool beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 in Iraola's first Champions League match
briefs.summary: Marcos Llorente put Atletico ahead in the 17th minute at Anfield before Dominik Szoboszlai leveled from close range on the stroke of halftime after a Ronald Araujo flick and Alexis Mac Allister won it in the 52nd with a 20-yard strike inside the left post. Andoni Iraola started Bradley Barcola and Rio Ngumoha; Cody Gakpo sat out with a minor adductor problem. Attendance was 59,466.

briefs.headline: Dodgers beat the Reds 14-1 to complete the sweep; De La Cruz homers a fifth straight game
briefs.summary: Yoshinobu Yamamoto held Cincinnati to three hits over seven innings with 10 strikeouts Wednesday at Dodger Stadium, and Rhett Lowder gave up seven runs on seven hits in 3 1/3 innings as Los Angeles scored six in the fourth. Elly De La Cruz's 26th homer, on Yamamoto's first pitch of the fourth, was the Reds' only run and made it a career-high five straight games with one; Mookie Betts, Max Muncy, Kyle Tucker and Enrique Hernandez homered for the Dodgers, who have won seven straight. The Reds are 69-77, fifth in the NL Central, and open at Milwaukee Friday at 7:45 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Pirates beat the White Sox 4-2 on a three-run seventh and reach .500
briefs.summary: Opener Lake Bachar and six relievers held Chicago to eight hits Wednesday at Rate Field; Brett Eisert got the win with 2 1/3 hitless innings and five strikeouts, and Mason Montgomery his 11th save. Enmanuel Valdez homered for Pittsburgh's first run in the fifth and Konnor Griffin drove in two in the seventh off Sean Newcomb; Munetaka Murakami's 31st homer accounted for one Chicago run. The Pirates are 73-73, third in the NL Central, with Jared Jones facing Hagen Smith in the finale at 7:40 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Union beat FC Cincinnati 5-0 after Nwobodo's 16th-minute red card
briefs.summary: Obinna Nwobodo was sent off on a VAR review in the 16th minute Wednesday at Subaru Park and Cincinnati played the rest a man down: Quinn Sullivan scored a 43rd-minute penalty, Bruno Damiani a hat trick in the 45th, 49th and 61st, and Milan Iloski a late penalty. It is Cincinnati's second straight shutout loss after the 4-0 at Nashville on Aug. 30. FCC are 8-8-7 with 31 points and host Charlotte on Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: D.C. United beat the Crew 2-1 on two first-half goals by Baribo
briefs.summary: Tai Baribo scored in the 24th and 36th minutes at Audi Field Wednesday, his 13th and 14th of the season, and Santiago Rodriguez answered in the 49th from Josef Martinez and Mohamed Farsi for Columbus, which is 6-13-5 with 23 points. Rodriguez has scored in each of his first two regular-season matches for the Crew; it was Martinez's first goal contribution for the club. The Crew host the Red Bulls Saturday at 7:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Chase, Higgins and Stewart are full participants on the Bengals' first injury report
briefs.summary: Wednesday's Week 1 report lists Ja'Marr Chase (knee), Tee Higgins (foot) and rookie end Shemar Stewart (knee) as full participants. Zac Taylor said the receivers 'continue to do more and more every day, but I like the pace they're on' and are on track for Sunday; on Stewart, 'I won't make any prediction how it's going to end up this week for him. I think he's feeling a lot better every single day.' Tampa Bay held out running back Sean Tucker (hamstring). Kickoff at Paycor Stadium is Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX.

briefs.headline: Browns list four as limited or full and hold nobody out before Jacksonville
briefs.summary: Cleveland's Wednesday report has center Parker Brailsford (thumb), tackle Maliek Collins (quad) and guard Teven Jenkins (back) limited and linebacker Carson Schwesinger (shoulder) full; Jacksonville held out running back LeQuint Allen Jr. (hip) and limited receiver Jakobi Meyers (thumb). The opener at EverBank Stadium is Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS.

briefs.headline: Rodriguez held a staff meeting 'while I was still pissed off' after the opener
briefs.summary: Rich Rodriguez said it was one of the first times he has met with his staff directly after a game, and that West Virginia 'had bad eyes more than bad angles' in the second half against Coastal Carolina; Michael Hawkins Jr. had 132 passing and 103 rushing yards and Cam Cook 142 yards and two touchdowns on 30 carries. Tennessee-Martin visits Saturday at 1 p.m. ET on ESPN+ in the first meeting between the schools.

briefs.headline: Pochettino calls the September camp 'a fresh start'; the roster comes Sept. 17
briefs.summary: Mauricio Pochettino will name 26 players on Sept. 17 for the U.S. men's national team's four home friendlies, opening with Peru in Orlando on Sept. 26, then Chile, Mexico and Canada. 'The headline needs to be a new start, a fresh start,' he said. 'The project is 2030.'

sections.label: Around the Leagues

briefs.headline: Hoshoryu skips practice a second day; his Aki entry is decided Friday morning
briefs.summary: Yokozuna (grand champion) Hoshoryu missed morning practice Wednesday and Thursday for medical appointments and has taken no bouts since his July 29 right-knee surgery; stablemaster Tatsunami said all he has managed is stomping shiko and giving his chest in butsukari-geiko (pushing drills). Kyodo says the decision comes at Friday morning's bout-drawing meeting in Tokyo, Thursday evening in the East; sitting out would be a third straight basho (tournament) missed and his first day-one withdrawal. Chunichi Sports calls his chances of entering 'extremely difficult.' The basho opens Sunday at Ryogoku Kokugikan, three days out.

briefs.headline: Kirishima closes his tune-up by winning 19 of 24 at Arashio stable
briefs.summary: Ozeki (champion) Kirishima, on a yokozuna promotion run, called his own final visiting practice Thursday in Tokyo and took 24 straight bouts against new sekiwake (junior champion) Fujinokawa, komusubi Daieisho and maegashira Abi, winning 19; after one loss to Daieisho he shouted for one more and won it. He said his movement and the sharpness of his charge 'weren't as good as yesterday,' when he won 19 of 21, and that all he can do now 'is rest well and go into the tournament.'

briefs.headline: Seahawks beat the Patriots 13-10 in the NFL opener as Maye throws three fourth-quarter interceptions
briefs.summary: New England led 10-3 entering the fourth quarter Wednesday night at Lumen Field; Drew Lock, in for Sam Darnold after Darnold hurt a hip on Seattle's sixth snap, found Jaxon Smith-Njigba for a 45-yard fourth-down touchdown to tie it, Julian Love's interception set up Jason Myers' 26-yard field goal and Josh Jobe's pick with 26 seconds left ended it. Drake Maye was 23-of-33 for 178 yards with a touchdown and three interceptions; Smith-Njigba had eight catches for 122 yards. The 49ers and Rams play tonight in Melbourne at 8:35 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Brewers beat the Cubs 8-6 to take the series and lead the NL Central by 10
briefs.summary: Christian Yelich's three-run homer in the first and homers by Jackson Chourio and William Contreras in the second put Milwaukee up 6-0 Wednesday at American Family Field, and a five-run Chicago ninth fell short. Logan Henderson went five innings on two hits for the win and Kevin Gausman took the loss after allowing six runs in four. The Brewers are 91-56 and the Cubs 81-66, 10.0 back and holding the second NL wild card.

briefs.headline: Phillies beat the Astros 11-7 on Schwarber's grand slam, his 44th homer
briefs.summary: Kyle Schwarber's 406-foot slam off AJ Blubaugh on a full count capped a six-run sixth Wednesday at Citizens Bank Park after Philadelphia trailed 4-0 and 6-4; it was his 10th career grand slam and his major-league-leading 44th homer. Cristopher Sanchez allowed six runs on 10 hits in six innings, Trea Turner homered, and Jose Altuve recorded his 2,500th hit for Houston. The Phillies, 82-64, are three behind Atlanta in the NL East and hold the top NL wild card.

briefs.headline: Arsenal beat Napoli 1-0 on Odegaard's goal in a night of 25 Champions League goals
briefs.summary: Martin Odegaard's 75th-minute low shot went in off the post Wednesday in Naples as Arsenal had 26 shots and 4.05 expected goals, both club records in the competition; Mikel Arteta said 'the performance doesn't reflect the result.' Elsewhere, Paris Saint-Germain beat Slovan Bratislava 6-1 on a Ferran Torres hat trick, Barcelona beat Feyenoord 5-1 with two from Raphinha, Stuttgart beat Viking 3-1 and Sporting beat Galatasaray 3-1.

briefs.headline: U.S. Open women's semifinals are tonight with all four top seeds still in
briefs.summary: No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka, seeking a third straight title, plays No. 3 Jessica Pegula and No. 2 Elena Rybakina plays No. 4 Coco Gauff on Thursday night at Arthur Ashe Stadium; Gauff came through three sets against Mirra Andreeva and Rybakina against Zheng Qinwen in Wednesday's quarterfinals. Friday's men's semifinals are Ben Shelton against Frances Tiafoe and Alexander Zverev against Karen Khachanov.

sections.note: Sumo copy was read on Yahoo Japan article pages carrying Kyodo, Chunichi Sports, Sports Hochi, Sankei and Nikkan Sports reports from Wednesday and Thursday in Tokyo; the JSA's English pages, including the withdrawal list, returned errors all morning, which is expected before Friday's bout-drawing meeting, and no kyujo (withdrawal) has been announced for anyone. Ozeki Aonishiki, taped at the left ankle, won all 15 bouts against a third-division stablemate Wednesday and will not spar another sekitori before Sunday, saying 'there's no anxiety.' The Aki basho opens Sunday, Sept. 13, three days out, and runs through Sept. 27. Around the majors Wednesday: the Rays beat the Braves 7-2 to lead the Yankees by four in the AL East, the Orioles beat the Guardians 9-5 on an eight-run third, and the Mets beat the Marlins 15-14 after blowing an 8-0 lead. Sam Darnold's hip injury was not a fracture, Mike Macdonald said, with no further detail. Session times for the U.S. Open semifinals were not confirmed on an opened page.

prime.item: Limits page effective Sept. 2, read again this morning: an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length, one per day, harvest reported to the division; the Fisherman's Post September report, published Sept. 1 and nine days old, has Native Son on a steady dock-and-creek-mouth bite starting on topwater early.

Limits page effective Sept. 2: a 14-inch minimum and 20-inch maximum total length, three per day, with one fish over 26 inches allowed; neither Sept. 1 report singles them out, so this is the seasonal pattern, not a live report: grass edges and dock lights on the flood, which tonight runs into the 8:29 p.m. sound high.

Limits page effective Sept. 2: a 12-inch fork-length minimum and 15 per day; the Sept. 1 Fisherman's Post report opens with East Coast Sports reporting Spanish and bluefish from the surf and piers on casting jigs, and the bluefish table's footnote caps private anglers at three a day.

Limits page effective Sept. 2: a 14-inch minimum and 25-inch maximum total length, 10 per day, with one fish over 25 inches allowed; the Sept. 1 report has Surf City Pier's bottom fishing holding black drum, pompano and croakers.

going_out.item: Day 10 of the two-week window, which closes at 11:59 p.m. Monday, Sept. 14, four days out, under proclamation FF-27-2026, read in full again this morning: one fish per day, 15-inch minimum, one daily limit per person aboard a vessel, no harvest under a Recreational Commercial Gear License, and the harvest must be reported.

The early Canada goose season closes Sunday, Sept. 13, three days out, per the DNR's 2026-27 migratory bird summary: five a day and 15 in possession, in aggregate, with HIP registration required. The regular goose season does not open until Oct. 3.
going_out.publication: West Virginia Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary, September 2026 - January 2027

sections.note: Gauley season opens Friday, Sept. 11: the National Park Service whitewater page, updated Aug. 26, lists Corps releases from Summersville Dam on Sept. 11-14, 18-21 and 25-28 and Oct. 2-5, 9-12 and 17-18, and the park's Aug. 24 letter to Gauley boaters says Tailwaters Campground is closed Sept. 11-28 to add parking, that Mason's Branch access closes when its lot fills, and that Hills to Hills is the only permitted commercial shuttle. Gauley Fest runs Sept. 17-20 at Nicholas County Veterans Memorial Park in Summersville per American Whitewater. The Forest Service posted a new closure Tuesday: Forest Road 19, the Dolly Sods road in the Cheat-Potomac district, closes for 5.3 miles from FR 75 east to County Road 28 from 6 a.m. Sept. 14 through 6 p.m. Sept. 25 for construction, through traffic prohibited; the FR 76 Cranberry River Road closure through Nov. 20 is unchanged. The Marine Fisheries limits page is still the one effective Sept. 2; the proclamation index moved and the version served this morning was a partial list, so nothing new was found rather than nothing issued. The DNR's stocking page lists no waters stocked, and its press-release index shows nothing newer than July 29. The first Chief Logan elk tour is Sunday, Sept. 13, per the DNR's Aug. 28 release; National Hunting and Fishing Day at Stonewall Resort is Sept. 19.

waters.working: Down from 69.9 cfs at this hour yesterday and about as low and clear as the river gets in September. At 48 cfs this is a long-leader, small-fly river: a 12-foot leader to 6X, a size 16 or 18 caddis or a small stonefly nymph through the pocket water and the plunge pools, caddis, stoneflies and sculpin being the forage, and a small olive sculpin along the undercut banks before the sun is on the water. NWS Charleston's 2:31 a.m. discussion has rounds of showers and storms ahead of a cold front through early Friday with flash flooding the main concern in training storms; the gridded forecast for Cowen sums to about half an inch today and under a third of an inch Friday, so the river should stay fishable unless a storm trains over the headwaters.
waters.note: No alerts were in effect for Webster County at 5:40 a.m. The Forest Service alerts page has nothing new on FR 86 or Tea Creek; the Aug. 12 campground bridge alert still stands, and the new Sept. 9 closure order is for FR 19 at Dolly Sods, Sept. 14-25, not the Williams. FR 76, the Cranberry River Road, stays closed in sections through Nov. 20.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 25.1 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The gauge read normal pool at 5 a.m., but the water is about to change: NWS Charleston issued a flash flood warning for northern Mason County including Point Pleasant, Leon, Henderson and Lakin at 3:10 a.m. and extended it at 5:39 a.m. to 8:15 a.m., saying 3 to 4 inches had fallen with up to an inch more possible. The Kanawha and the small tributaries on both banks will put color into the pool side through the weekend. Before it arrives, this is still structure water: shad are the forage, so a white or pearl swimbait over the wing-dam tips at first light, then a football jig dragged into the slack behind them; once the creeks come in, the bite moves to the mudlines where a colored creek meets the clearer pool.
waters.note: This is the pool side, 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam. USGS does not gauge the Byrd tailwater, and the Corps' Huntington District site refused the connection this morning on a certificate mismatch, so no lock or navigation notice is printed. The NWS has no forecast point at Point Pleasant; Huntington is the forecast gauge.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 25.8 ft and falling — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: The Weather Service reissued the Huntington forecast at 10:25 a.m. Wednesday, and it now has a modest rise instead of the slow fall it carried Tuesday: 26.0 feet by 8 a.m. today, 26.3 by Friday morning and a 26.8-foot crest early Saturday, falling back to 26.1 by Monday, no flooding, with the action stage at 48 feet. That is a foot of rise over two days, enough to put current on the lock wall and color along the banks. Shad and skipjack are the forage, so a skipjack-pattern swimbait or a white spinnerbait along the riprap and the lock wall early today while it is still clear, and a crawfish-colored jig in the slack behind the barge cuts and the wing-dam tips as the river comes up.
waters.note: This is the gauge below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam, not the tailwater. The Corps' Huntington District site could not be reached, so no lock notice is printed. The NWS forecast was issued before Wednesday night's rain over Mason County and will likely be reissued today.

waters.reading: Sound highs 7:59 AM at 4.0 ft and 8:29 PM at 4.4 ft at Hampstead; lows 2:19 AM at 0.4 ft and 2:28 PM at 0.2 ft.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 7:59 AM and 8:29 PM in the sound.
waters.working: The Fisherman's Post September report, published Tuesday, Sept. 1 and nine days old, opens with East Coast Sports reporting Spanish mackerel and bluefish from the surf and piers on casting jigs, and inside has Native Son on a steady red drum bite at docks and creek mouths starting on topwater early and Carolina Flats on a strong class of 20-to-24-inch flounder with the mullet thick; no October report has been filed. Reds want the last of the fall, which runs into the 2:28 PM low in the sound; flounder on the first of the flood at the creek mouths, then the push into the 8:29 PM high for trout on the grass edges. New moon is tonight at 11:27 p.m. ET, per the U.S. Naval Observatory, so these are spring tides: the biggest swings of the month and the hardest inlet current, with the most bait moving. Water 80.2F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast.
waters.note: NWS Wilmington's 2:56 a.m. surf forecast has a moderate rip current risk for Pender beaches from 6 a.m. through this evening, surf around 2 feet, a southwest wind 5 to 10 mph turning south 10 to 15 in the afternoon, a low waterspout risk today and moderate Friday, and a heat index to 103 Friday. No coastal flood advisory is in effect for Pender or New Hanover. The National Hurricane Center's 2 a.m. Atlantic outlook expects no tropical cyclone formation in the next seven days. Hampstead is the sound station and the read that matters; the oceanfront pier runs well ahead and is quoted only for a surf read.
